title: Linux_Remaiten_Botnet_Investigation_255
description: Investigate and identify malicious activity, determine its scope, and recommend containment measures for the Linux/Remaiten botnet.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The network has experienced unusual traffic patterns and potential unauthorized access. Your task is to investigate and identify any malicious activity, determine its scope, and recommend containment measures.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Host: victim (192.168.80.100)
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario. Use the following credentials to access the victim host:
- Host: victim (192.168.80.100)
- Username: ubuntu
- Password: ubuntu

Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Investigate Unusual Traffic Patterns
levels.content: Investigate the unusual traffic patterns on the victim host. What service is responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic?
levels.solution: Check the running services and look for any unusual or unfamiliar services. The correct service name is 'bot-flood.service'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the running services and look for any unusual or unfamiliar services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the systemctl command to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service' to list all running services.

levels.title: Determine the Target of Abnormal Network Traffic
levels.content: Determine the target of the abnormal network traffic. What is the IP address of the system receiving the abnormal volume of network traffic?
levels.solution: Examine the network connections and logs related to the suspicious service. The correct IP address is '192.168.80.100'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the network connections and logs related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the ss command to list all network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run the command 'ss -tulnp' to list all network connections.

levels.title: Investigate the Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Investigate the persistence mechanism of the suspicious service. How is the suspicious service automatically started after a reboot?
levels.solution: Look for systemd timers or other scheduling mechanisms that might be responsible for starting the service. The correct persistence mechanism is 'systemd timer'.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for systemd timers or other scheduling mechanisms that might be responsible for starting the service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the systemctl command to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Run the command 'systemctl list-timers' to list all systemd timers.
